newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada's Alberta to shift priorities -premier.
newsitem.headline: Canada's Alberta to shift priorities -premier.

text.p: Ralph Klein, premier of the Canadian province of Alberta, said on Tuesday his government planned to shift priorities to job creation and managing economic growth from its long-established policy of debt and deficit control.

Klein, in a television address to the province in advance of an expected spring election, offered few details on how he would stimulate job creation, although he said he would soon release a new human resources strategy for Alberta.

In the speech, Klein defended the intensity of his fiscal programme, which since 1993 has resulted in government spending cuts of 20 percent, and said he would keep tight controls on the public purse. "Never again will lenders and rating agencies direct the future of our province," he said.

Although Klein did not specifically update Alberta's projected 1996/97 budget surplus, he did forecast a C$2.2 billion debt repayment. Provincial law requires all budget surplus to be applied to the accumulated debt.
Alberta's economy has been bolstered over the past two years by a revitalised oil and gas industry, as well as strong activity in other sectors such as agriculture, manufacturing and forestry.

He said savings on interest through debt repayment would free up C$400 million for "reinvestment" into education, health care, social services and public works, where most of the past cuts have been made.
